steps.do: Click “Continue with a wallet”, choose MetaMask and approve the sign-in message in the wallet.

notes.text: Never approve a deposit in the wallet (“Add funds”): the app's server sends it on to a real testnet. Rejecting one is fine.
Don't use Mint or any faucet: it is rate-limited and the account has what it needs.

The account is kept between runs and holds a short Google position, deposits waiting in a queue and many old orders. Leave them alone; a test only touches what it made itself, and trades Apple (AAPL/USD).

Before the first order, the order button reads 'Enable trading' and asks for a one-time eth_signTypedData_v4 DelegationAuth (pod delegation) signature; the order button only appears after that is signed.

There is no Market/Limit switch: typing into the Price field turns the order into a Limit order, and the refresh icon next to it puts the mid price back. Leverage and TP/SL are hidden behind 'More options›'.
Close, Edit and Set TP/SL for a position are on Home: expand its Holdings row and they appear as links to the market page. The account already holds a Google short, so look for Apple rows only.
Withdraw is in the Account menu (avatar, top right). The per-deposit Withdraw buttons on Home belong to old queued deposits: leave them alone.
The Orders list does not update by itself after placing or cancelling an order: reload the page to see the new row or its Cancelled status.
After every page reload the order button reads “Enable trading” again, and the first Cancel click asks for a new DelegationAuth signature, so approve it in the wallet.
Position value on Home includes the existing Google short (about $45), so only its change is meaningful.
Closing: Home Apple row > Close Apple opens the market page; click Enable trading (sign DelegationAuth), then All, then Close long. Reload to see Orders update.
The account's buying power is large, so $900,000 at 5× trips the limit; the limit figure in the message (about $398k) changes with the balance, so don't assert it.
Nothing is created by this test, so there is nothing to clean up.
Withdraw is in the Account menu (avatar); the per-deposit Withdraw buttons on Home are for old queued deposits, not this dialog.
Position opened from the order panel shows Leverage 19.96× and Margin used $2.45 on Home regardless of the 5× chosen under More options.
Market order size for $50 comes out at 0.1372 AAPL (~$49), sized at a price about 2% above mid, so match 'about $50', not exactly 50.

tests.name: Place a $50 Long limit order on Apple well below mid and see it rest open
tests.goal: A user with cash places a $50 Long limit order on Apple at $300, well below the mid price. It shows in the Orders list as a resting (open) Buy limit at $300.00 and does not fill.

steps.do: Click “Enable trading” and approve the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet

run.note: Click "Enable trading" to start the one-time DelegationAuth signature

steps.do: Make sure the “Long” tab is selected and the amount unit is “USD”, then type 50 into the Amount field (placeholder “0.00”)

run.note: Make sure the Long tab is selected

steps.do: Type {{limit}} into the Price field

steps.claim: The Price field shows {{limit}}, the form describes it as a Limit order that rests until the price is reached, and the badge next to the price reads "BELOW MID" (the price is below the mid price)

steps.do: Click the “Long AAPL/USD” button

run.note: Place the $50 long limit order at {{limit}}

steps.claim: The order button shows “Order submitted” (a confirmed notice appears)

steps.do: Reload the page /trade/AAPLUSD:perp so the Orders list refreshes (the list does not update by itself)

steps.claim: The first row of the Orders list is a BUY LIMIT at ${{limit}}.00 for AAPL placed “just now” (or seconds ago) with status Open and Modify / Cancel buttons — it is not Filled and not Cancelled
The Orders list shows no Filled row placed just now for AAPL at ${{limit}}.00, so the limit order did not fill

steps.do: In the Orders list, click “Cancel order” on the first row (the Open BUY LIMIT at ${{limit}}.00) and approve the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet if one appears
Reload the page /trade/AAPLUSD:perp

steps.claim: The first row of the Orders list is the BUY LIMIT at ${{limit}}.00 and its status is Cancelled, and no row in the Orders list is still Open

cleanup.do: On the Apple (AAPL/USD) market page, cancel every open AAPL order in the Orders list that is a Buy limit with status Open, using its Cancel button, and approve the delegation signature in the wallet if asked

tests.name: Open a $50 Long on Apple at 5× and see it under Holdings
tests.goal: A user opens a $50 market Long on Apple (AAPL/USD) at 5× max leverage. The order shows as Filled, and an Apple LONG position of matching size shows up under Holdings on Home, with Position value and Margin available changed to match.

steps.do: Click “More options›” in the order panel

run.note: Open More options in the order panel

steps.do: Click “5×” under “Max leverage”
With “Long” selected and the amount in USD, type 50 into the amount field (placeholder “0.00”)
Click “Enable trading” and approve the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet

run.note: Enable trading to get the DelegationAuth signature request

steps.claim: The wallet was asked for the DelegationAuth signature

steps.do: Click “Long AAPL/USD”
Reload the Apple page (/trade/AAPLUSD:perp) so the Orders list refreshes

steps.claim: The first row of the Orders list is a BUY MARKET order on AAPL with status Filled, placed “just now” or within the last minute, and its size is about 50 dollars worth of AAPL at that row's price (roughly 0.137 AAPL at about $357)

steps.do: Click “Home” in the left rail

run.note: Open Home from the left rail

steps.claim: Under Holdings, there is an Apple PERP AAPL/USD row marked LONG whose size is about 0.137 AAPL and whose Value is about $49 to $50 (the $50 order)
Position value at the top equals the sum of the Values of the rows under Holdings (the Apple long plus the existing Google short), within about a dollar, and Margin available is lower than Cash

steps.do: Click the Apple row under Holdings to expand it

run.note: Expand the Apple row under Holdings

steps.claim: The expanded Apple row shows the position was opened at 5× leverage: Leverage reads about 5× and Margin used is about one fifth of the position Value (about $10)

steps.do: Click “Close Apple” in the expanded Apple row
On the Apple market page, click “Enable trading” and approve the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet
Click “All” in the Close position panel, then click “Close long”
Open Home again and confirm the Apple row is gone from Holdings, leaving only the Google short

cleanup.do: Close any open Apple (AAPL/USD) long position: on Home expand the Apple row, click Close Apple, click Enable trading and approve the DelegationAuth signature, click All, then click Close long. Leave the Google short and the queued deposits alone.

tests.name: Over-leverage Apple Long is refused
tests.goal: A user enters a $900,000 Apple Long at 5× max leverage and is told 'Over your 5x limit … raise Max leverage or lower the amount'. No order is placed.

steps.do: Click “Enable trading” and approve the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet

run.note: Click Enable trading to start the DelegationAuth signature

steps.do: Click “More options›” to show the leverage settings
Click the “5×” button under “Max leverage”
Type 900000 into the Amount field (USD)

steps.claim: The order form shows a red message that starts with “Over your 5x limit” and ends with “raise Max leverage or lower the amount”
The order button “Long AAPL/USD” is disabled
The wallet was not asked to sign any order or transaction after the DelegationAuth signature

tests.name: Reject Enable trading signature on Apple
tests.goal: A user who clicks Enable trading on the Apple page and rejects the signature in the wallet sees the button go back to Enable trading, and no order is placed.

steps.do: Click “Enable trading” and reject the DelegationAuth signature request in the wallet.

run.note: Start trading enablement so the DelegationAuth signature request appears

steps.claim: The wallet was asked for a DelegationAuth signature, and that was the only signature request.
The order button reads “Enable trading” again and is not stuck on “Enabling trading…”.
No order was placed: the wallet was asked to sign no order, and the page shows no order confirmation.

tests.name: Withdraw more than the withdrawable balance is refused
tests.goal: A user types a withdrawal of $90,000, more than the $79,598 available, and sees 'amount exceeds your withdrawable balance' with Continue disabled.

steps.do: Click "Account" in the top right, then click "Withdraw" in the menu

run.note: Open Withdraw from the Account menu

steps.claim: The withdraw dialog asks "How much would you like to withdraw?" and shows a "Max available" figure

steps.do: Type 90000 into "Withdraw amount"

steps.claim: The page shows the message "amount exceeds your withdrawable balance"
The "Continue" button is disabled
The wallet was not asked to sign anything
